Check a Marker Panel for Data Quality Issues

Source: R/checkPanel.R
checkPanel.Rd

Performs a comprehensive diagnostic check of a raw marker genotype matrix and its associated genetic map, reporting data quality issues without modifying the data. The results guide the choice of thresholds for the subsequent filterPanel step.

The following checks are performed:

Encoding validation

Confirms that genotype values lie within the expected range for the stated encoding.

Map consistency

Identifies markers present in geno but absent from map (unplaceable) and vice versa.

Duplicate lines

Lines with identical genotype profiles.

Duplicate markers

Markers with identical genotype profiles across all lines.

Marker missingness

Per-marker proportion of missing genotypes.

Line missingness

Per-line proportion of missing genotypes.

MAF distribution

Per-marker minor allele frequency; summary statistics and a table showing how many markers would be removed at standard thresholds (0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10).

Monomorphic markers

Markers with MAF = 0 that carry no information.

Heterozygosity

Per-line proportion of heterozygous calls. Excess heterozygosity may indicate mixed or mislabelled samples.

Chromosome coverage

Number of markers and position range per chromosome (in the same units as the map.pos column).

Usage

checkPanel(
  geno,
  map,
  id = "id",
  map.id = "marker",
  map.chr = "chr",
  map.pos = "pos",
  encoding = "012"
)

Arguments

geno

A numeric matrix (lines x markers) with row names identifying lines, or a data.frame with a column named by id identifying lines and remaining columns containing marker genotypes.

map

A data.frame containing the genetic map with at minimum three columns: marker names (map.id), chromosome identifiers (map.chr), and marker positions (map.pos). Positions may be in any consistent unit — cM for a genetic map, or Mb, kb, or bp for a physical map.

id

Character string naming the line identifier column when geno is a data.frame. Ignored when geno is a matrix. Default "id".

map.id

Character string naming the marker column in map. Default "marker".

map.chr

Character string naming the chromosome column in map. Default "chr".

map.pos

Character string naming the marker position column in map. Positions are used as supplied — no unit conversion is applied. Default "pos".

encoding

Character string specifying the genotype encoding: "012" (default, allele counts 0/1/2 or dosage in [0,2]) or "pm1" (already in additive \(\pm 1\) coding).

Value

An object of class "checkPanel" — a list containing:

$geno

The original (unmodified) genotype matrix.

$map

The original (unmodified) map data frame.

$encoding, $id, $map.id, $map.chr, $map.pos

Arguments as supplied, carried through for filterPanel.

$n.lines, $n.markers, $n.chr

Dimensions of the panel.

$encoding.ok

Logical; FALSE if values lie outside the expected range.

$consistency

List with $not_in_map and $not_in_geno: character vectors of marker names.

$dup.lines

Character vector of duplicate line IDs (the second and subsequent copies).

$dup.markers

Character vector of duplicate marker names (the second and subsequent copies).

$miss.marker

Named numeric vector of per-marker missing rates.

$miss.line

Named numeric vector of per-line missing rates.

$maf

Named numeric vector of per-marker minor allele frequencies (computed on markers present in both geno and map).

$maf.table

Data frame showing the number and percentage of markers removed at standard MAF thresholds.

$monomorphic

Character vector of monomorphic marker names (MAF = 0).

$het

Named numeric vector of per-line heterozygosity rates.

$het.marker

Named numeric vector of per-marker heterozygosity rates.

$chr.coverage

Data frame with columns chr, n.markers, pos.min, pos.max; positions are in the same units as the map.pos column.
